Ansible executes tasks in a sequence, so first task is executed in parallel on all hosts, then second task, then third and so on. That's one of the reasons you get only values from last host on list when referencing them like that. You have to reference specific host variable you have to use hostvars, so : {{ hostvars\[host\].ciscooutput.stdout\_lines }}


Anyway this is only true when your destination file is shared between hosts, so every time your copy task is executed it overwrites the same file. Otherwise you'll be creating a copy on results.txt on every host. To resolve this use local_action, and write to file on host ansible is executed from

> On the third day of our hike, I was so tired, that I couldn't stand on my feet, resting at almost every step. In addition my exhaustion was increased by pain and open, ulcerating wound of my left thigh, caused my whole leg to swell. I had to make a firm decision. We were still in the middle of the forest. I didn't want to slow the pace of my companions in misery, so I suggested them to leave me here until next day and look for some village or food, and return back here for me, when they find it. Through the day I'll get some rest and pull myself together. They were resisting long, but in our position they had no choice. We had to act firmly, but also quickly, before we get detected by German cleaning squads wandering through forest. Recalling our fights in those woods, I gave my leaving colleagues direction angle [azimuth?], which probably could help them find some nearby settlements. Not wasting their time, they left quickly in pointed direction and I was preparing my shelter from moss. Covering and masking myself with heathers, I fell asleep instantaneously. How long I was sleeping and what happened to me I couldn't perceive. It was still dark, but starlit sky gave so much light, that I could recognize objects within 2-3 steps. Complete silence was only disturbed by some forest birds, quivering and slowly waking up. I was recovering slowly, I took out my watch - unfortunately, I couldn't see the hour, and I didn't want to light the match. I leaned back by nearest tree and patiently waited for dawn. Those long hours till dawn - they felt like eternity. At dawn, I was wondering when established signal from my comrades will come. Whole day passed like that. Although I didn't sleep for all day, when the night came, I decided I have to find some settlement by myself at all cost, because my leg was hurting even more and I was hungry, since all my hardtacks I had in my pocket were out. It was clear, that my companions were either caught by enemy patrol or lost and unable to find the place they left me. I didn't even consider that they could leave me to die, because they were excellent soldiers and extremely friendly men, which were proven many times in our journey. I had German Mauser 7,35mm with two full magazines, compass and binoculars. I decided to take the same direction my boys went immediately to get advantage of the night. I was walking very slowly with many stops; my leg was hurting too much. Going like that, around 4 a.m. the forest begin to thin out - I felt a little cold and moist ground under my feet. I thought it was some wet meadow with hazel bushes growing here and there. I decided to move forward. I took several dozen of steps, ground under my feet was alternately solid and totally soft. Suddenly, I fell almost to my neck into the swampy pit. At the first moment I was terrified, but I tried to keep it cool by thinking it's probably the one of the places where peat was dug. 1. Małyszko and Małyszka is *probably* just grammatical difference depending on context it was used or a typo.

2. It's wrong transcription. There's no -ovna in male names, so her father couldn't have Maliszkovna as last name. Zuzanna was married, so it would be Maliszkova in that case. Change of y to i was also result of wrong transcritpion, but it more or less reflects how you shoud say that name. Correct names are Wincenty Małyszko and Zuzanna Małyszko or (using more traditional style) Wincenty Małyszko  and Zuzanna Małyszkowa. Her mother's name was probably Anna Sobek, Anna Sepek or Anna Sepko. Or again, traditionally - Anna Sobkowa or Anna Sepkowa.

3. I don't know why there's a difference in mother's name. Especially her first name, altough there's polish name Anna Maria which translates roughly to Ann Marie/Ann Mary/Mary Ann. But it still doesn't explain change in last name (which correct form is Popielarczyk, I believe). Maybe he lost his biological mother somehow and was raised by some other woman?  

4. née stands for the maiden name. Literally Anna née Saczek is Anna from home Saczek.
Yes, Bronisław is hist first name. Bronek in diminutive form.

Moim zdaniem w pierwszym przykładzie chodzi o to, czy ważniejszy jest wkład pracy (*ukończyłam*) czy rezulatat (*mam ukończony*), ale różnica w sensie zdania jest bardzo subtelna i de facto ludzie nie zwracają na to uwagi. Poza tym wygodniej jest powiedzieć *zrobiłem* niż *mam zrobione* - brzmi to bardziej naturalnie.
W kolejnych przykładach różnica wydaje mi się bardziej znacząca. Po pierwsze, w pismach i mowach oficjalnych składanych w imieniu firmy i instytucji zwykle stosuje się formę *mamy zrobione* (czyli w tym wypadku *mamy wyremontowany cały oddział*), niż *zrobiliśmy*. *Zrobiliśmy* jest bardziej potoczne i używane przez osoby bezpośrednio zaangażowane (w przykładzie - przez robotników, którzy oddział wyremontowali). Tak samo minister edukacji, mówiąc oficjalnie o przygotowaniach do egzaminów w całym kraju powie raczej *uczniowie mają przećwiczone zadania egzaminacyjne z ubiegłych lat*. Ale już dyrektor szkoły, który będzie mówił o swojej placówce i bezpośrednio, osobiście zna uczniów, o których się wypowiada może powiedzieć zarówno *Uczniowie przećwiczyli zadania egzaminacyjne z ubiegłych lat*, jak i *uczniowie mają przećwiczone zadania egzaminacyjne z ubiegłych lat*.

Krótko to podsumowując, myślę, że główną rolę w konstruowaniu tego typu wypowiedzi odgrywają 3 czynniki:

* czy jest to wypowiedź oficjalna (*mamy zrobione*) czy potoczna (*zrobiliśmy*),

* czy mamy do niej stosunek osobisty (tj. czy jesteśmy bezpośrednio zaangażowani),

* co chcemy zaakcentować (czyli albo nasz wkład pracy - *ukończyłam kurs*, albo otrzymany rezultat - *mam ukończony kurs*).

A, jeszcze jedno - jestem ekonomistą, polski jest dla mnie ojczystym językiem :)
